subject.title: [Feature]: Supports Windows 11 MSYS environment and Fishshell.

question: Should `install.sh` officially support Windows MSYS2/MINGW plus fish PATH persistence, or should OpenClaw keep routing Windows Unix-like users to WSL2/PowerShell?
rationale: The source path is clear, but accepting MSYS2/MINGW is a Windows platform support commitment with installer/package-manager and shell-profile implications that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Approve scoped MSYS2/fish support
options.body: Implement MSYS2/MINGW detection, safe install decisions, fish PATH persistence or guidance, docs, tests, and real Windows smoke proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Document MSYS2 as unsupported
options.body: Keep the supported Windows paths as Windows Hub, PowerShell, and WSL2, update docs or installer copy if needed, then close this request as out of scope.

options.title: Split fish from MSYS2
options.body: Handle fish PATH guidance as a narrower installer UX task while separately deferring the MSYS2/MINGW support decision.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped MSYS2/fish support
recommendation.body: Implement MSYS2/MINGW detection, safe install decisions, fish PATH persistence or guidance, docs, tests, and real Windows smoke proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete posted the prior product-boundary review and recently touched the public Windows/install docs that would define the support decision.
